Marco Jansen to Josh Hazlewood, out Caught by Aiden Markram!! It's a comeback for the ages from South Africa as they level the series in Gqeberha. Captain Temba Bavuma's incredible rescue act, Marco Jansen's all-round efforts, the fire of Rabada and the persistence of Mulder have conjured up a win that will occupy its place among their most memorable ones. And once again, after the familiar highs of Durban, Australia get another taste of the dirt in Gqeberha like they did in 2014 and 2018. Jansen it is who has the honour of putting the finishing touches. Short of length outside off, climbs on Hazlewood as he looks to cut and flies off the edge into the safe hands of Markram at second slip. The celebrations begin in the crowd and on the field. Josh Hazlewood c Aiden Markram b Marco Jansen 0(2)

Pat Cummins | Australia captain 1/2: [How do you sum up today’s defeat?] I feel there was some good fight today. Scotty Boland and Trav both, I thought played their roles really well. But, yeah, it was a fair way to come back from it. Wasn't quite enough. [What was missing compared to the Durban performance?] I think it was a lot. Yeah, obviously a long way away from our best. I think last week we didn't start off too strong, but everyone contributed, and lots of little things added up to a win. But, yeah, today, just across the board, not enough of us contributed. [How difficult is it to get the team balance right?] I think the balance is always fine. We're lucky we've got loads of all-rounders to call on, so I don't think that's a major issue. But, yeah, again, kind of from all departments, just needed a little bit more.

Bavuma 2/4: [How do individual performances make your job easier as captain?] Makes the job a lot easier. I mean, a guy like KG, just his value that he brings in, his ability to assume the responsibility and pressure from the bowling attack and kind of allow the other guys to do what they naturally can do. You saw a guy like Marco Jansen in the first innings coming through with his class, and even in the second innings as well. So he's of massive value. I think for him (Rabada), he'll have the cobwebs. He would have dusted those off. It's been a while since he was out on the field, but due to the guy's class, you know, he's still able to go and get four wickets in the second innings. So, yeah, hopefully that continues to get better and better.

Bavuma 3/4: [How did you keep the team focused despite the rain delays?] I think it's just basically to try to stay in the moment, right? Like, I think when we were batting, for me, it was all about how we can extend it, how we can go another hour. Another hour becomes a session. How we can make sure we keep them on their feet, because we know how that does have an effect. And then, once the opportunity is there, we'll be calling on us to be a lot more ruthless. And I think in the second innings, that's exactly what we did. So I think that's how we play our cricket. I think our team, the way we go about it, we play good old Test cricket, try and wear the opposition down and then take them down when the opportunity presents itself.

Bavuma 4/4: [How will South Africa manage Anrich Nortje’s absence in Cape Town?] I mean, that's a big loss for us. We know what an extra dimension he adds to our bowling attack. I think that one we do have to take it upon ourselves. We probably took the risk by allowing him to play two games in a row. So, I think that's just for us to take on. In terms of who might come, obviously, we'll go to Cape Town. We'll see what's happening there in Cape Town. You've got guys like Gerald (Coetzee) on the wings, Dane Paterson as well as (Corbin) Bosch. So, I mean, the options are there. There's Sean (Senuran Muthusamy) as well. But, yeah, the options are there. Whoever we decide after we're there in Cape Town, we'll be confident that they form part of our best XI for those conditions.

Plenty to ponder for Australia with their batting issues being brutally exposed in the last couple of days. Some of the shot-selection left a lot to be desired and a couple of their players seem to be in a rut. Marnus Labuschagne has now gone over three years since his last hundred, and 14 innings since his last fifty, while Nic Maddinson looks out of sorts at the top of the order. How long before they pull the trigger on a change or two? Then there's the dilemma about Nathan Lyon, and who makes way if he returns. Surely you can't leave Scott Boland out after this performance, surely... South Africa, on the other hand, will be pumped. The return of KG Rabada has been a huge boost and while Nortje may not be available in Cape Town, there are suitable replacements to call on. What a decider it promises to be. Can't wait.
